extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate / graduate students and instructors in commutative algebra
extracted.subtask_description: Collection of exercise statements and solution-sketches from a commutative algebra textbook (sections on completions, Noetherian rings, DVRs, Dedekind domains, fractional ideals, valuation rings). Each rubric item is an exercise / proposition stating hypotheses and the property to prove, with surrounding solution guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: p-adic completion of A equals A
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A := ⊕_{n} Z/⟨p⟩ (the direct sum of copies of Z/p) and B := ∏_{n} Z/⟨pn⟩ with the natural map φ: A → B. Show that the p-adic completion bA is just A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solution note: pA = 0 so every Cauchy sequence in A is eventually constant; hence A is already complete (bA = A). (This is used as part (1) of a three-part exercise showing failure of right-exactness of completion.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of A in topology induced from B
rubrics_metrics.description: With A and B as above and A given the subspace topology induced from the p-adic topology on B, show that the completion of A in this induced topology equals the product ∏_{n} Z/⟨p⟩ (i.e., the full product rather than the direct sum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define fundamental neighborhoods Ak = φ^{-1}(p^k B); show Ak = ⊕_{n>k} ⟨p^k⟩ = ⟨p^k⟩-components and deduce the completion is lim_k A/Ak ≅ ∏_{n} Z/⟨p⟩. Use general facts about completions and inverse limits (22.6) and projections.

rubrics_metrics.name: p-adic completion not right-exact
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that the natural sequence of p-adic completions 0 → bA → bB → b(B/A) is not exact at bB for the A and B above (so p-adic completion is not right-exact on the category of Z-modules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine (1) and (2). Since bA = A but the completion of A in the induced topology is strictly larger (uncountable), the image of bA in bB does not equal the kernel of b(B)→b(B/A). Conclude Im(bφ) ≠ Ker(bψ).

rubrics_metrics.name: M ↦ cM preserves surjections; surjectivity of bR ⊗ M → cM
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R be a ring and a an ideal. Show the functor M ↦ cM (completion or separated completion) preserves surjections, and that the natural map bR ⊗_R M → cM is surjective when M is finitely generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the first part of the proof of (22.14) showing preservation of surjections; then apply (8.16) to deduce surjectivity of the stated map when M is finitely generated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal property descends from completed ring
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R be Noetherian, a and b ideals, and assume a ⊂ rad(R). Using the a-adic topology, prove b is principal if b·bR is principal (i.e., principality of bR implies that of b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since R Noetherian, b is finitely generated. Use that a ⊂ rad(R) and Nakayama-type arguments: b = a b is cyclic if b·bR is cyclic, apply (10.11)(2), (22.9) and (22.19)(2) to pass between b and bR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nakayama’s Lemma for complete rings
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R be a ring, a an ideal, and M an R-module. Assume R is a-complete and M is separated (a-adic). Show that elements m1,...,mn ∈ M generate M if their images generate M/aM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: consider associated graded modules G(M), G(R) and use prior result (22.23) that generation on graded pieces lifts. Alternative approach: use completeness and separatedness to identify M = cM and use surjectivity of R → bR and properties of ba ⊂ rad(bR) to apply Nakayama (10.11)(2) over bR, then descend to R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion preserves Noetherian/local/regular properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m. Prove (1) bA is Noetherian local with maximal ideal bm, (2) dim(A) = dim(bA), and (3) A is regular iff bA is regular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) Use (22.26) for Noetherian and (22.8) for locality. (2) Use equality of powers A/m^n = bA/bm^n and dimension results (20.13),(21.4). (3) Compare minimal number of generators of m and bm using (22.9) and (10.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequence for M-sequences: divisibility property
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R be a ring, M a module, and x,y ∈ R. (1) If x,y form an M-sequence, then given any m,n ∈ M with x m = y n there exists p ∈ M with m = y p and n = x p. (2) Converse holds if R is local, x,y ∈ m (maximal ideal), and M is Noetherian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solution sketch: For (1) reduce modulo xM and use nonzerodivisor property of y on M/xM. For (2) construct descending chain of submodules using successive p's and use Noetherian property to force vanishing; then deduce divisibility and nonzerodivisor condition on residues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permutation invariance of M-sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R local with maximal ideal m, M Noetherian, and x1,...,xn ∈ m form an M-sequence. Show any permutation of x1,...,xn is also an M-sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to adjacent transpositions: show xi, xi+1 forming an M_{i-1}-sequence implies xi+1, xi do too (use the prior divisibility lemma (23.6)), then proceed by composing transpositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular local ring characterized by existence of A-sequence generating m
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be Noetherian local of dimension r ≥ 1. Prove A is regular iff its maximal ideal m is generated by an A-sequence (i.e., m has a regular sequence of length r generating it).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If A regular, choose regular system of parameters and inductively show they form an A-sequence using domain and prior results. Conversely, if m is generated by an A-sequence then depth and dimension inequalities give equality n = r so A is regular.

rubrics_metrics.name: DVR is maximal proper subring of its fraction field; localization changes dimension
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be a DVR with fraction field K, and f ∈ A a nonzero nonunit. Prove A is a maximal proper subring of K and that dim(A) ≠ dim(A_f) (indeed A_f = K has dim 0 while A has dim 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given any ring R with A ⊊ R ⊆ K, pick x ∈ R ackslash A, write x = u t^n with uniformizer t and u∈A*, n<0, construct y ∈ A such that t^{-1} ∈ R, then deduce R = K. For dimension, localizing at f gives Af = K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local DVR criterion for plane curve singularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Let k field, P = k[X,Y], f irreducible with f = ℓ(X,Y)+g, ℓ linear, g ∈ ⟨X,Y⟩^2. For R = P/⟨f⟩ and p = ⟨X,Y⟩/⟨f⟩, show Rp is a DVR iff ℓ ≠ 0 (i.e., the plane curve f=0 is nonsingular at (0,0)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute m/m^2; if ℓ ≠ 0 then m/m^2 is 1-dimensional so m principal and domain ⇒ DVR; if ℓ = 0 then m/m^2 is 2-dimensional so not a DVR. Use Nakayama and earlier DVR criteria (23.9,23.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermediate local ring between k[X] and k[[X]] is a DVR
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be a ring with k[X] ⊆ A ⊆ k[[X]], local with maximal ideal ⟨X⟩. Prove A is a DVR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show the intersection of ideals ⟨X^n⟩ in A is zero (it is in k[[X]]), then apply (23.3) or DVR characterization to conclude A is DVR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prime height preserved under algebraic field extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L/K algebraic extension and P and Q polynomial rings over K and L respectively. (1) For q prime of Q and p = q ∩ P, show ht(p)=ht(q). (2) If f,g ∈ P have no common prime factor in P then they have no common prime factor in Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) Use integrality Q is integral over P and going-down/incomparability or compare transcendence degrees via (15.12) and (15.13). (2) If f,g had a common prime q in Q, localize at q to get a DVR and contract to P to contradict no common factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced Noetherian rings characterized by (R0) and (S1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R be Noetherian. Show R is reduced iff it satisfies (R0) and (S1) (Serre conditions: R0 = minimal primes are fields; S1 depth≥1 off minimal primes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If (R0) and (S1) hold, then in an irredundant primary decomposition each associated prime is minimal, with qi = pi and radical of zero is intersection of primes so ⟨0⟩ is reduced. Conversely, reduced ⇒ localizations Rp reduced ⇒ (R0), and from associated primes properties deduce (S1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Normality via principality of height-1 associated primes
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R Noetherian domain. Show R normal iff for every prime p associated to a principal ideal, pRp is principal (equivalently Rp is DVR for such primes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If R normal, localize at primes and use (23.9). For converse, use Serre's criterion: show (R1) and (S2) by checking height-1 primes and depth-1 localizations become DVRs, hence normal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation between height-1 primes and depth-1 primes; exact sequence to detect S2
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R Noetherian, K its total quotient ring. Let set A = {p prime | ht(p)=1} and B = {p prime | depth(Rp)=1}. Assuming (S1) show A ⊆ B and prove A = B iff (S2) holds. Without assuming (S1), show canonical sequence R → K → ∏_{p∈B} Kp/Rp is exact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use existence of nonzerodivisors in primes of height 1 to place them in Ass(R/⟨x⟩) and deduce depth1. For exactness, take x=a/b ∈ K which maps to zero in each Kp/Rp and deduce a ∈ bR via associated primes and (18.25). Use these facts to relate A and B and S2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalences characterizing normal Noetherian rings (Dedekind-style criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Noetherian R, prove equivalence of (1) R normal, (2) (R1) and (S2) hold, and (3) (R1) and (S1) hold and the sequence R → K → ∏_{p:ht p=1} Kp/Rp is exact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1)⇒(2): standard. (2)⇒(3) trivial. (3)⇒(1): integral elements lying in each Rp for height-1 p must lie in R by exactness; combined with reducedness (from (S1)) gives normality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimension of localization for one-dimensional domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R domain, S multiplicative. (1) If dim(R)=1 then dim(S^{-1}R)=1 iff there exists a nonzero prime p with p ∩ S = ∅. (2) More generally, dim(R)=1 iff dim(Rp)=1 for every nonzero prime p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use correspondence of primes under localization (11.18) and chains of primes to compare dimensions; specialise to localizations at multiplicative sets avoiding a nonzero prime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization of Dedekind domains yields Dedekind domains iff prime avoided
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R be Dedekind, S multiplicative. Show S^{-1}R is Dedekind iff there is some nonzero prime p with p ∩ S = ∅.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such p exists then S^{-1}R is domain, Noetherian, normal and dimension 1 by previous facts (24.5). Conversely use (24.5)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distributive laws for ideals in Dedekind domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R Dedekind and a,b,c ideals. Prove a ∩ (b + c) = (a ∩ b) + (a ∩ c) and a + (b ∩ c) = (a + b) ∩ (a + c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Localize at each maximal ideal (localization commutes with sums/intersections) to reduce to DVR case; in a DVR ideals are ⟨t^i⟩ and the identities reduce to min/max formulas for integers i,j,k.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semilocal Dedekind domain is a PID
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that a semilocal Dedekind domain A (finitely many maximal ideals) is a PID by proving each maximal ideal is principal and then using the Main Theorem of ideal theory to write any ideal as a product of principal maximal ideals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Chinese Remainder Theorem to construct elements with prescribed congruences to force a generator for a given maximal ideal; then factor arbitrary ideals as products of principal maximal ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideals in quotient by ideal of Dedekind domain are principal; two-generator property
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R be Dedekind and a,b nonzero ideals. (1) Every ideal in R/a is principal. (2) Any ideal b is generated by two elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Localize away from associated primes of a to make the quotient semilocal and a PID, then lift back to R/a using localization and Chinese Remainder; for (2) pick x∈b nonzero, find y whose residue generates b/⟨x⟩ to get b=⟨x,y⟩.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal fractional ideal equivalence and canonical maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R domain, M a fractional ideal. Prove M is principal iff there exists an isomorphism M ≅ R. Construct canonical surjection M ⊗ N → MN and canonical isomorphism φ:(M:N) → Hom(N,M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If M ≅ R send 1↦ generator. For maps: define multiplication map (x,y)↦xy to get M⊗N → MN; define φ(z)(y)=yz for z∈(M:N) to get Hom(N,M) and show injective/surjective using a nonzero element of N.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor product isomorphism when M locally principal
rubrics_metrics.description: Let M locally principal fractional ideal. Prove the natural map M ⊗ N → MN is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check after localizing at each maximal ideal m: Mm is principal so Mm ⊗ Nm ≅ MmNm and use (13.20) to globalize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invertible fractional ideals in a UFD are principal
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R a UFD. Show a nonzero fractional ideal M is invertible iff M is principal and nonzero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonzero principal ideals are invertible. Conversely, if M invertible write 1 = ∑ m_i n_i with m_i∈M, n_i∈M^{-1}; pick nonzero m∈M and construct gcd-based argument to show M = R x for some x.

rubrics_metrics.name: PID characterization: Dedekind + UFD
rubrics_metrics.description: Show R is a PID iff it is a Dedekind domain and a UFD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PID ⇒ Dedekind and UFD. Conversely, a Dedekind UFD has every nonzero fractional ideal invertible (25.3,25.13) hence principal by UFD property (25.11), so PID.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invertible modules are finitely generated and locally free rank 1 in local case
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R ring and M invertible module. Prove M is finitely generated, and if R is local then M is free of rank 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an explicit presentation from the inverse module N and the evaluation isomorphisms; show a finite generating set exists from the decomposition of 1 in R via pairing, and in local case produce an element m with a splitting map to show M ≅ R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent characterizations of invertible modules and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Show for an R-module M the following are equivalent: (1) M invertible; (2) M finitely generated and Mm ≅ Rm for each maximal ideal m; (3) M locally free of rank 1. Deduce M finitely presented and M ⊗ Hom(M,R) ≅ R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1)⇒(2) via localization and (25.16). (2)⇔(3) via (13.28). Use local freeness to obtain finite presentation (13.27) and identify evaluation map ev: M⊗Hom(M,R)→R, checking it is an iso locally and hence globally by (13.20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation ring ideal-chain criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Let V be a domain. V is a valuation ring iff for any two ideals a and b either a ⊆ b or b ⊆ a (i.e., ideals are totally ordered by inclusion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If V valuation ring then for nonzero x,y, one of x/y or y/x lies in V, giving containment on principal ideals; conversely, the total order on ideals forces for x,y nonzero either x|y or y|x so V is valuation ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization of valuation rings at primes
rubrics_metrics.description: Let V valuation ring, m maximal ideal and p ⊆ m prime. Show V_p is a valuation ring, its maximal ideal equals p (i.e., p V_p = p), and V/p is a valuation ring of the field V_p/pV_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with fractions in Frac(V) and check valuation property passes to localization; check ideals in localization and primeness to verify equalities; reduce to checking nonunits and images modulo p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation rings are normal
rubrics_metrics.description: Show any valuation ring V is integrally closed (normal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If x ∈ Frac(V) is integral over V and not in V then 1/x ∈ m (maximal ideal) so the integral equation yields 1 ∈ m, contradiction. Hence x ∈ V.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximal local subrings of K are valuation rings
rubrics_metrics.description: Let K field and S the set of local subrings of K ordered by domination. Show maximal elements of S are precisely the valuation rings of K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If V maximal, by (26.9) it is dominated by some valuation ring V' so maximality forces equality. Conversely, valuation rings are maximal because any dominating local ring would have to coincide by valuation characterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archimedean-valued valuation rings are maximal subrings of K
rubrics_metrics.description: Let V valuation ring whose value group is Archimedean. Show V is a maximal proper subring of its fraction field K (i.e., any strictly larger ring equals K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If R strictly contains V pick a∈R ackslash V with v(a)<0, and for any b∈K find n such that v(b a^n) > 0 by Archimedean property so b a^n ∈ V, hence b ∈ R. Conclude R = K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finitely generated ideals in valuation rings are principal; Noetherian iff DVR
rubrics_metrics.description: Let V valuation ring. (1) Every finitely generated ideal is principal. (2) V is Noetherian iff V is a DVR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) For a = ⟨x1,...,xn⟩ pick xi with minimal valuation; others are multiples of xi so a=⟨xi⟩. (2) If Noetherian then maximal ideal principal hence DVR (23.9); conversely DVR is PID hence Noetherian.
